1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 AP_SPINLOCK-backed software hwspinlock.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h>
12: 
13: #include "arm_internal.h"
14: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
15: 
16: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY       0xa1000000u
17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 && (bk7258_boottrace_words()[6] & 0xffu) == 2u)
39:     {
40:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */
93: 
94:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
95:   UP_DMB();
96:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
99: 
100:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
101:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
102:     {
103:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
104:       UP_DMB();
105:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
106:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
112:   UP_DMB();
113:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
114:   return true;
115: }
116: 
117: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
118: {
119:   (void)dev;
120:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
121: }
122: 
123: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
124: {
125:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
126: 
127:   (void)dev;
128:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
129:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
130:     {
131:       PANIC();
132:     }
133: 
134:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
135:     {
136:       UP_DMB();
137:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
138:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
143:   UP_DMB();
144:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
145:   UP_DSB();
146:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
147:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
148: }
149: 
150: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
151: {
152:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
153:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
154:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
155: };
156: 
157: void bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize(void)
158: {
159:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[0] = 0;
160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
164:   UP_DSB();
165:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
166: }

69:     {

82:  *   This function disables context switching by disabling addition of
83:  *   new tasks to the g_readytorun task list.  The task that calls this
84:  *   function will be the only task that is allowed to run until it
85:  *   either calls  sched_unlock() (the appropriate number of times) or
86:  *   until it blocks itself.
87:  *
88:  * Input Parameters:
89:  *   None
90:  *
91:  * Returned Value:
92:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure
93:  *
94:  ****************************************************************************/
95:

97: void sched_lock(void)
98: {
99:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
100: 
101:   /* Catch attempts to increment the lockcount beyond the range of the
102:    * integer type.
103:    */
104: 
105:   DEBUGASSERT(rtcb && rtcb->lockcount < MAX_LOCK_COUNT);
106: 
107:   /* A counter is used to support locking. This allows nested lock
108:    * operations on this thread (on any CPU)
109:    */

111:   if (rtcb->lockcount++ == 0)

52: /****************************************************************************
53:  * Name:  nxsched_cpu_scheduler
54:  *
55:  * Description:
56:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
57:  *   active task on one CPU.
58:  *
59:  * Input Parameters:
60:  *   cpu - The CPU that we are performing the scheduler operations on.
61:  *
62:  * Returned Value:
63:  *   None
64:  *
65:  ****************************************************************************/
66: 
67: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
68: static inline void nxsched_cpu_scheduler(int cpu)
69: {
70:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
71: 
72: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
73:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses round robin scheduling. */
74: 
75:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
76:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR)
77:     {
78:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
79:        * timeslice.
80:        */
81: 
82:       nxsched_process_roundrobin(rtcb, 1, false);
83:     }
84: #endif
85: 
86: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
87:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses sporadic scheduling. */
88: 
89:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
90:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
91:     {
92:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
93:        * budget.
94:        */
95: 
96:       nxsched_process_sporadic(rtcb, 1, false);
97:     }
98: #endif
99: }
100: #endif
101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name:  nxsched_process_scheduler
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
107:  *   active task on all configured CPUs.
108:  *
109:  * Input Parameters:
110:  *   None
111:  *
112:  * Returned Value:
113:  *   None
114:  *
115:  ****************************************************************************/
116: 
117: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
118: static inline void nxsched_process_scheduler(void)
119: {
120:   irqstate_t flags;
121:   int i;
122: 
123:   /* Single CPU case:
124:    * For nested interrupts, higher IRQs may interrupt nxsched_cpu_scheduler()
125:    * but nxsched_cpu_scheduler() requires that interrupts be disabled.
126:    * We are in ISR context, no meaning we are disabled the interrupts.
127:    *
128:    * SMP case:
129:    * enter_critical_section() does much more than just disable interrupts on
130:    * the local CPU; it also manages spinlocks to assure the stability of the
131:    * TCB that we are manipulating.
132:    */
133: 
134:   flags = enter_critical_section();
135: 
136:   /* Perform scheduler operations on all CPUs */
137: 
138:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; i++)
139:     {
140:       nxsched_cpu_scheduler(i);
141:     }
142: 
143:   leave_critical_section(flags);
144: }
145: #else
146: #  define nxsched_process_scheduler()
147: #endif

214: {
215:   FAR sq_entry_t *entry;
216: 
217:   sq_for_every(hold_spinlock, entry)
218:     {

220: #  ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK_BACKTRACE

222:       FAR void **stack;

227:       _alert("Spinlock(%p) backtrace: %s\n", info, buf);

234: void spinlock_mark_locking(FAR spinlock_debug_t *info)
235: {
236:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = running_task();
237: 
238:   /* Since it is not allowed to call enter_critical_section while holding
239:    * spinlock, it destroys the deadlock condition of waiting in a loop.
240:    * So no mark is required.
241:    */
242: 
243:   if (info == &g_schedlock.info)
244:     {
245:       return;
246:     }
247: 
248:   /* Check if the current tcb is not waiting for other spinlock. */
249: 
250:   if (rtcb->wait_spinlock != NULL)
251:     {
252:       _alert("Detect thread(%d) is waiting for multiple spinlocks at the "
253:              "same time, lock1(%p) and lock2 (%p)!\n",
254:              rtcb->pid, rtcb->wait_spinlock, info);
255:       dump_spinlock(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
256:       PANIC();
257:     }
258: 
259:   /* Only the method of acquiring lock through busywait needs to be marked.
260:    * If the lock is acquired through trylock, no marking is required
261:    * because it will not cause a circular wait and lead to deadlock.
262:    */
263: 
264:   rtcb->wait_spinlock = info;
265: }
266: 
267: void spinlock_mark_locked(FAR spinlock_debug_t *info)
268: {
269:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = running_task();
270: 
271:   /* Since enter_critical_section allows lock context switching and
272:    * repeated locking, no mark is required.
273:    */
274: 
275:   if (info == &g_schedlock.info)
276:     {
277:       return;
278:     }
279: 
280:   /* Check if the spinlock has been held. */
281: 
282:   if (info->holder != NULL)
283:     {
284:       _alert("Detect thread(%d) relocks spinlock(%p)!\n",
285:              rtcb->pid, info);
286:       dump_spinlock(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
287:       PANIC();
288:     }
289: 
290:   /* Check if the current tcb acquires the right lock. */
291: 
292:   if (rtcb->wait_spinlock != info)
293:     {
294:       _alert("Detect thread(%d) wants to acquire lock1(%p), but ends up "
295:              "acquiring lock2(%p)!\n",
296:              rtcb->pid, rtcb->wait_spinlock, info);
297:       dump_spinlock(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
298:       PANIC();
299:     }
300: 
301:   /* Set info and enqueue. */
302: 
303:   info->holder = rtcb;
304:   spinlock_add_backtrace(info);
305:   sq_addlast(&info->flink, &rtcb->hold_spinlock);
306: 
307:   /* Reset wait_spinlock. */
308: 
309:   rtcb->wait_spinlock = NULL;
310: }
311: 
312: void spinlock_mark_unlocked(FAR spinlock_debug_t *info)
313: {
314:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = running_task();
315: 
316:   /* Since enter_critical_section allows lock context switching and
317:    * repeated locking, no mark is required.
318:    */
319: 
320:   if (info == &g_schedlock.info)
321:     {
322:       return;
323:     }
324: 
325:   /* Check if locking and unlocking are the same task. */
326: 
327:   if (info->holder != rtcb)
328:     {
329:       _alert("Detect thread(%d) unlocks spinlock(%p) which is not held!\n",
330:              rtcb->pid, info);
331:       dump_spinlock(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
332:       PANIC();
333:     }
334: 
335:   /* Currently, NuttX does not support unlock in the reverse order, since
336:    * this will pollute flags. So check if unlocking is the reverse order.
337:    */
338: 
339:   if (sq_tail(&rtcb->hold_spinlock) != &info->flink)
340:     {
341:       _alert("Detect thread(%d) unlocks spinlock(%p) in the wrong order!\n",
342:              rtcb->pid, info);
343:       dump_spinlock(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
344:       PANIC();
345:     }
346: 
347:   /* Reset info and dequeue. */
348: 
349:   info->holder = NULL;
350:   spinlock_remove_backtrace(info);
351:   sq_remlast(&rtcb->hold_spinlock);
352: }

127:  ****************************************************************************/
128: 
129: clock_t nxsched_process_roundrobin(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, clock_t ticks,
130:                                    bool noswitches)
131: {
132:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;  /* Pointer to the next ready-to-run TCB */
133:   clock_t ret;
134:   int decr;
135: 
136:   /* How much can we decrement the timeslice delay?  If 'ticks' is greater
137:    * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138:    *
139:    * 'ticks' should not be greater than the remaining timeslice.  But that
140:    * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been
141:    * disabled or the noswitches flag is set.  This might cause jitter of a
142:    * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.
143:    */
144: 
145:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL);
146:   decr = MIN(tcb->timeslice, ticks);
147: 
148:   /* Decrement the timeslice counter */
149: 
150:   tcb->timeslice -= decr;
151: 
152:   /* Did decrementing the timeslice counter cause the timeslice to expire? */
153: 
154:   ret = tcb->timeslice;
155:   if (tcb->timeslice <= 0 && !nxsched_islocked_tcb(tcb))
156:     {
157:       /* We will also suppress context switches if we were called via one
158:        * of the unusual cases handled by nxsched_reassess_timer().  In that
159:        * case, we will return a value of one so that the timer will expire
160:        * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161:        * timer expiration context.
162:        *
163:        * This is kind of kludge, but I am not to concerned because I hope
164:        * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165:        * rare corner-cases.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (noswitches)
169:         {
170:           ret = 0;
171:         }
172:       else
173:         {
174:           /* Reset the timeslice. */
175: 
176:           tcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
177:           ret = tcb->timeslice;
178: 
179:           /* We know we are at the head of the ready to run prioritized
180:            * list.  We must be the highest priority task eligible for
181:            * execution.  Check the next task in the ready to run list.  If
182:            * it is the same priority, then we need to relinquish the CPU and
183:            * give that task a shot.
184:            */
185: 
186: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
187:           ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
188: #else
189:           ptcb = tcb->flink;
190: #endif
191:           if (ptcb &&
192:               ptcb->sched_priority >= tcb->sched_priority)
193:             {
194:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
195: 
196:               /* Just resetting the task priority to its current value.
197:                * This will cause the task to be rescheduled behind any
198:                * other tasks at the same priority.
199:                */
200: 
201: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
202:               DEBUGASSERT(tcb->task_state == TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING);
203:               if (tcb->cpu != this_cpu())
204:                 {
205:                   nxsched_smp_call_init(&g_call_data,
206:                                         nxsched_roundrobin_handler,
207:                                         (FAR void *)(uintptr_t)tcb->pid);
208:                   nxsched_smp_call_single_async(tcb->cpu, &g_call_data);
209:                 }
210:               else if (nxsched_switch_running(tcb->cpu, true))
211: #else
212:               if (nxsched_reprioritize_rtr(tcb, tcb->sched_priority))
213: #endif
214:                 {
215:                   nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
216:                 }
217:             }
218:         }
219:     }
220:   else if (tcb->timeslice == 0)
221:     {
222:       ret = CLOCK_MAX;
223:     }
224: 
225:   return ret;
226: }
227: 
228: #endif /* CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 */

43:  * Description:
44:  *    This function is used to process the tcb in g_delivertasks.
45:  * 1 We use direct locking instead of enter_critical_section
46:  * to save processing time
47:  * 2 If there is a higher priority task, we will still perform
48:  * the higher priority task
49:  * 3 If the schedule lock is on, the task will be placed in g_pendingtasks
50:  *
51:  * Input Parameters:
52:  *   cpu
53:  *
54:  * Returned Value:
55:  *   OK
56:  *
57:  * Assumptions:
58:  * - The caller must be in irq
59:  * - current cpu must not be locked
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: void nxsched_process_delivered(int cpu)
64: {
65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;
67: 
68:   DEBUGASSERT(up_interrupt_context());
69: 
70:   flags = enter_critical_section();
71:   priority = per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu);
72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;
73: 
74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&
75:       !nxsched_switch_running(cpu, priority == SWITCH_EQUAL))
76:     {
77:       /* Manage the (rare) case that task delivery to this CPU was not
78:        * successful. This can happen in two cases:
79:        * 1) The currently running task on this CPU just entered sched_lock
80:        * 2) This CPU just picked a higher priority task to execute
81:        *    before this SMP call was executed
82:        * To avoid schedule latency/priority inversion, just check once more
83:        * if there is another CPU eglible to run the delivered task, and
84:        * pass it forward.
85:        */
86: 
87:       FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
88:       if (tcb)
89:         {
90:           int target_cpu = tcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ?
91:             tcb->cpu : nxsched_select_cpu(tcb->affinity);
92:           if (target_cpu != cpu &&
93:               current_task(target_cpu)->sched_priority < tcb->sched_priority)
94:             {
95:               nxsched_deliver_task(cpu, target_cpu, priority);
96:             }
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:   leave_critical_section(flags);
101: }

<thinking>**Evaluating possible circular waits**</thinking>
The scheduler lock is a global recursive `rspinlock` in this SMP (non-BMP) build. Acquiring it performs short atomic gate transactions, then releases the gate; while holding the scheduler lock, later `atomic_read`/CAS operations reacquire the gate, giving a concrete `scheduler lock -> atomic gate` nesting, but not a continuously held `atomic gate -> scheduler lock` nesting in the ordinary APIs.

# Deadlock-chain investigation report

Scope: `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing`, with the corresponding NuttX tree at `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx`. Investigation was read-only.

## Configuration identity

The active CMake build is the two-CPU SMP configuration:

- `CONFIG_SMP=y`, `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=2`:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:420-425`
- `CONFIG_SPINLOCK=y`, `CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK=y`:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:411-412`
- `CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_HWSPINLOCK=y`:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:1373`
- `CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH` is disabled:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:595-600`

The older `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config` reports `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=1` and `CONFIG_LIBC_ATOMIC_TOOLCHAIN=y` at lines 407 and 1049. That is a stale/different build configuration and must not be mixed with the active `cmake_out` result.

## Actual call and lock paths

### Timer path

The BK7258 timer ISR executes:

```text
bk7258_timerisr
  -> bk7258_smp_retry_pending
  -> nxsched_process_timer
```

Evidence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:39-53`
- SysTick is enabled only by `bk7258_timer_start()`, which rejects non-CPU0 callers:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:63-75`
- CPU1's private SysTick is explicitly disabled:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:82-96`

`nxsched_process_timer()` executes, in order:

```text
clock_timer()
nxsched_process_scheduler()
wd_timer()
```

Evidence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_processtimer.c:179-200`

`clock_timer()` takes the system-tick seqlock:

```text
up_irq_save()
atomic_read(&sequence)
atomic_cmpxchg(&sequence, ...)
g_system_ticks++
atomic_store_release(&sequence, ...)
up_irq_restore()
```

Evidence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/clock/clock_initialize.c:462-471`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/seqlock.h:150-175`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/seqlock.h:194-200`

Because `CONFIG_SMP` is enabled, those seqlock atomic operations use the libc atomic backend.

### Libc atomic path

The generated atomic functions in `arch_atomic.c` all follow this pattern:

```text
atomic_lock()
  -> hwspin_lock_irqsave(&g_atomic_hwspinlock)
  -> operation
atomic_unlock()
  -> hwspin_unlock_restore()
```

Evidence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:41-51`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:53-64`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:81-105`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:324-344`

The BK7258 atomic device is bound to the BK7258 gate:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_atomic.c:9-16`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/CMakeLists.txt:30-36`

`hwspin_lock_irqsave()` disables local IRQs before entering the potentially spinning lock and restores them only after unlocking:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h:95-113`

### BK7258 gate behavior

The gate is not a non-recursive lock. It tracks:

```text
owner
depth
interested[2]
turn
```

Evidence:

## Scheduler critical-section path

In the active SMP/non-BMP configuration, `enter_critical_section()` is:

```text
up_irq_save()
rspin_lock(&g_schedlock)
```

Evidence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:1535-1546`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:707-712`

`rspin_lock()` itself performs atomic reads/CAS operations. Each such atomic operation temporarily acquires the BK atomic gate, then releases it before `rspin_lock()` returns:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:666-704`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:53-64`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/libs/libc/machine/arch_atomic.c:81-105`

The scheduler lock is recursive by CPU:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:676-682`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:767-775`

The `g_schedlock` object is global rather than separately allocated per CPU because `CONFIG_BMP` is disabled:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:420-425`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/percpu.h:112-121`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/irq/irq_csection.c:44-46`

This creates the following practical nesting:

```text
enter_critical_section:
    local IRQ mask
    short atomic-gate acquisition(s)
    g_schedlock held
        later atomic operations may reacquire the atomic gate
    g_schedlock release
    IRQ restore
```

It does not hold the atomic gate continuously while acquiring or holding `g_schedlock`.

## `sched_lock()` is a different lock

`sched_lock()` does not acquire `g_schedlock`, does not acquire the BK atomic gate, and does not disable interrupts. It only increments the current TCB's `lockcount`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_lock.c:97-115`

Consequently:

- A thread holding only `sched_lock()` can be interrupted by SysTick.
- The timer path may enter `nxsched_process_scheduler()`.
- Round-robin switching is suppressed for a locked TCB by `nxsched_islocked_tcb()`:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_roundrobin.c:152-156`
- This is not a same-gate recursive deadlock.

`sched_unlock()` first enters a critical section and then performs atomic TCB flag reads while that scheduler critical section is held:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_unlock.c:58-61`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_unlock.c:88-109`

That is a concrete `g_schedlock -> atomic gate` usage, but the atomic gate is acquired only for individual operations.

## Can the timer ISR interrupt a thread holding the same gate?

### Normal SysTick case: no

The atomic gate is entered through `hwspin_lock_irqsave()`, which masks local interrupts first:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h:95-100`

On Cortex-M, this port implements `up_irq_save()` by raising `BASEPRI` to `NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/include/arm_m/irq.h:462-471`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/include/arm_m/nvicpri.h:71-74`

SysTick is configured at the default priority:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:88-92`

The active build does not enable high-priority interrupt handling:

- `CONFIG_ARCH_HIPRI_INTERRUPT` is unset:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:299-302`

Thus a normal SysTick cannot interrupt the local thread during the interval in which that thread owns the atomic gate.

### Same-CPU exceptional/high-priority case: qualified

If an exception were allowed to bypass the `BASEPRI` mask, the gate has explicit same-CPU recursion once `owner` has been published:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:64-75`

However, an interrupt occurring in the narrow Peterson acquisition window before `owner` is written at lines 94-110 would not necessarily take the recursion branch. That scenario is not the normal BK7258 SysTick configuration and is not established by the active configuration. It would require a bypassing exception or a direct non-`irqsave` caller.

## Conclusion

The claimed chain contains several real edges but does not form the asserted same-CPU deadlock:

```text
SysTick ISR
  -> nxsched_process_timer
  -> clock_timer
  -> short atomic gate acquisition
  -> nxsched_process_scheduler
  -> enter_critical_section
  -> g_schedlock
  -> short atomic gate acquisitions
```

A thread can hold `sched_lock()` and still be interrupted, but `sched_lock()` is only a scheduling/preemption lock. A thread holding the BK atomic gate acquired through the actual libc backend has local IRQs masked, so normal SysTick cannot interrupt it. If a same-CPU re-entry nevertheless occurs after gate ownership is published, `owner/depth` handles it recursively.

The source therefore does **not** substantiate the proposed deadlock cycle. It does substantiate short cross-CPU contention on the BK gate and scheduler-lock nesting around atomic operations. A separate deadlock would need an additional path that holds one persistent lock while synchronously waiting for another; none is present in the examined timer, libc atomic, scheduler, SMP-call, or BK gate paths.

**Confidence:** High, approximately **0.90** for normal active-build behavior and maskable SysTick semantics. Approximately **0.75** for excluding exceptional bypass paths such as NMI/HardFault or unshown board-specific code, because those are outside the ordinary `irqsave`/SysTick chain and are not demonstrated by this source set.
